author: ValWood
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**


GO:0008308 | voltage-gated monoatomic anion channel activity | IBA with Q586M2 , locus:2147820 , P42057 , locus:2158606 , locus:2100252 , MGI:106919 , P45880 , locus:2174517 , P21796 , S000005000 , FBgn0004363 , PTN000201897 , 621575


* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**

https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPAC1635.01
but all Mitochondrial outer membrane transporters

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**


Annotation.

Appears to be a biophysical property under artificial conditions, only observed in vitro for this class of proteins.
Its dramatic voltage sensitivity in bilayers led to the name.

However, the mitochondrial outer membrane  has little or no membrane potential. 
Also, the MOM acts more like a sieve (@hattrill  I think we discussed this earlier)

I looked at a couple of the papers associated with the above annotation, and the ones I looked at didn't even assay  the activity (I think the annotations are largely extrapolated from transport phenotypes and the unfortunate name).

For example the SGD annotation appears to be based on the evaluation of expression in E. coli 
https://www.jbc.org/article/S0021-9258(19)57825-5/fulltext


@Antonialock @hattrill  could you look at UniProt and fly annotations in the new year and see if you agree with this annotation?

I'm wondering if this involved in tRNA import (Note that it is related to Tom6)...it is still an open question whether some modified tRNAs that are detected in the mitochondria are imported, or  the  modification enzymes are imported (at present there is no evidence for some of the modifiers in the mitochondria). 


* Add the label 'high priority' if needed. Generally high priority issues affect a lot of proteins, and annotations are incorrect (as opposed to just imprecise).
title: PAINT issue: GO:0008308 | voltage-gated monoatomic anion channel activity | PTN000201897

rename.to: PAINT issue: GO:0008308 | voltage-gated monoatomic anion channel activity | PTN000201897

author: ValWood
body: This is complicated by the fact that in yeast, there is only one copy, and this appears to be only the mitochondrial outer membrane. In higher eukaryotes there alse appears to be some PM localization, and multiple copies. Will be difficult to unpick...

author: hattrill
ValWood
body:
OK, the tRNA transport was only a hunch (I'm looking for candidates because it isn't yet clear whether tRNAs can be exported to modify them, and reimported, although it seems like a bit of a palaver!).

Re the 'voltage -gated' I still can't find any evidence for a sustained membrane potential across the MOM  where this transporter is located (isn't it only the inner membrane that has  a stong membrane potential?) . Also yeast don't have   apoptosis.

I'm going to block PANTHER:PTN000201897 for pombe but if Mark thinks it is relevant I'm happy for this ticket to be closed with no action

author: hattrill
body:
> Re the 'voltage -gated' I still can't find any evidence for a sustained membrane potential across the MOM where this transporter is located (isn't it only the inner membrane that has a stong membrane potential?) . Also yeast don't have apoptosis.

At best it is hypothetical and would be limited to apoptosis. PMID:10781072. There is no solid answer, but blocking voltage-gating for yeast seems more than reasonable. No one seems to have really nailed this down, even now. 

> I'm going to block PANTHER:PTN000201897 for pombe but if Mark thinks it is relevant I'm happy for this ticket to be closed with no action

I don't think it would be a deal breaker if it weren't propagated by PAINT as porin activity would be the major, universal truth. I am ok with just annotating the v-g to the papers that show it.

author: marcfeuermann
body: This one is a complex one. It is a huge family and many members are also found at the plasma membrane, the vacuole membrane and even the mitochondrial inner membrane. Due to the high number of EXP data all over the family for the voltage-gate function I would keep it. I can propose to block it for fungi. Would this be okay for you ?

author: ValWood
body: No problem. The yeast one might be a problem, it isn't well characterised, and so even the location could be incorretc. Leave this one as it is for now. I wasn't sure about this one.

author: marcfeuermann
body: Okay, I'm closing this one, Can be reopened if necessary ;-)
